title: NFC Cosmetics Authentication Labels — Tap-to-Verify
summary: At BOM level, NFC cosmetics authentication labels embed {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} (AES-128 + Secure Dynamic Messaging) into ultra-compact 12 × 19 mm or Ø 18 mm flexible PET inlays that conform to curved bottle, compact, jar, and tube surfaces without detuning. They are the cryptographic anti-counterfeit layer for premium cosmetics (Estée Lauder, La Mer, SK-II, Chanel, Lancôme, K-beauty exporters), serums, fragrances, hair-care professional-only product, and refill-bottle resale verification — paired with EU Cosmetic Products Regulation 1223/2009 + CPNP notification reference and US MoCRA 2022 facility registration framework on the consumer-tap branded page. Premium-cosmetics brand-protection teams can use it as the chip / inlay-size / curved-surface / regulatory-coexistence reference.

brief.label: Chip silicon options
items: {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} ({chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:partNumber}): AES-128 + Secure Dynamic Messaging — per-tap unique CMAC URL; the cryptographic authentication tier.
NXP NTAG213 (marketing-only variant): smartphone-readable static URL; for consumer-engagement programmes without anti-counterfeit requirement.
Choose NTAG 424 DNA for any premium / counterfeit-targeted product; NTAG213 only for engagement-only marketing labels with no authentication claim.

brief.label: Inlay size and form factor
items: Ø 18 mm round: serum / foundation bottle bottom or neck band, jar bottom or lid insert, compact base.
12 × 19 mm rectangular: compact / palette inside lid, tube body label or crimp seal, lipstick / lip-gloss tube.
Ø 22 mm round: fragrance bottle bottom, outer-packaging box flap seal (with tamper-evident adhesive variant).
Custom sizes 4-8 weeks for specialised packaging where standard footprints don't fit.

brief.label: Substrate and curved-surface compatibility
items: Flexible PET film substrate conforms to curved bottle and tube surfaces without detuning the NFC antenna.
Maintains reliable read performance on cylindrical / oval containers — the structural advantage over rigid inlays.
Transparent PET overlay + clear adhesive minimises visual impact on clear / transparent packaging.
Aluminium antenna pattern subtly visible on close inspection but blends into most packaging designs; embed under opaque label or inside packaging structure for fully invisible placement.

brief.label: Adhesive options
items: Permanent adhesive: standard for under-bottom-label and inside-lid placements.
Tamper-evident adhesive: leaves 'VOID' pattern on attempted removal; standard for outer-packaging / box-flap seal.
Repositionable: development-only / sample placement; not for production deployment.

brief.label: Read distance by inlay size
items: Ø 22 mm round: 25-35 mm from modern smartphone — fragrance bottle bottom, outer box.
Ø 18 mm round: 20-30 mm — serum / foundation bottle, jar bottom, compact base.
12 × 19 mm rectangular: 15-25 mm — compact / palette / tube body.
Ø 12 mm round (smallest standard): 5-10 mm — lipstick / lip-gloss / micro-SKU; below this size first-tap reliability drops below the 95% threshold for consumer-facing deployments.

brief.label: Counterfeit cosmetics market context
items: Counterfeit beauty market estimated >USD 5B annually; fakes widely sold on mainstream e-commerce, social-media marketplaces, physical stores.
Counterfeit cosmetics frequently contain lead, mercury, arsenic, bacteria, unregulated ingredients — direct consumer-safety hazard.
Single contaminated batch sold under genuine brand label generates product-liability lawsuits, regulatory investigations, lasting brand-safety damage even though brand manufactured nothing harmful.
Visual replication near-parity with genuine — packaging quality alone no longer distinguishes counterfeit from genuine.

brief.label: EU Cosmetic Products Regulation 1223/2009 + CPNP
items: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 — every cosmetic product placed on EU market must be notified to Cosmetic Products Notification Portal (CPNP).
On-pack disclosures required: Responsible Person identity, INCI ingredient list, batch code, PAO (Period After Opening) symbol — must remain on physical packaging; NFC tag does not substitute.

NFC adds: extended-information layer (full INCI with allergen highlighting, safety-assessment summaries, CPNP notification reference), batch-level recall targeting under Article 6 post-market surveillance, Responsible Person contact path for Article 23 SUE (serious undesirable effects) reporting.
CPNP notification ID encoded in SDM payload — consumer page cross-references against EU public CPNP lookup.

brief.label: US MoCRA 2022 (Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act)
items: FDA-administered facility registration, product listing, safety substantiation, adverse-event reporting — the first major modernisation of US cosmetics regulation since 1938.
MoCRA establishes adverse-event reporting requirements for serious adverse events within 15 business days.
NFC adds consumer-facing complaint / adverse-event reporting flow on the branded tap page.
Facility-registration ID can be encoded in SDM payload for FDA traceability cross-reference.

brief.label: Refill-bottle anti-counterfeit
items: Premium fragrance + skincare refill bottles a documented counterfeit vector — counterfeiters source genuine bottles, refill with inferior product.
NFC under-bottom or neck-band placement + tamper-evident adhesive on outer-box seal makes refill detection possible.
Bridge-antenna closure variants (analogous to spirits cap-bridge) for premium fragrance bottles — opening breaks antenna trace.
Resale verification on premium beauty resale platforms (Poshmark, Mercari, Glambot) — same chip serves first-buyer + second-buyer.

brief.label: Consumer engagement post-verification
items: Ingredient transparency: full INCI list, sourcing, safety certifications, allergen highlighting.
How-to tutorials: video tutorials showing correct application techniques for the specific product.
Reorder: one-tap link to repurchase from brand e-commerce store.
Loyalty points: award loyalty points or rewards for each verification tap.
Batch recall: if a batch is recalled, the tap alerts the consumer immediately — backend recall targeting through the verification database.

brief.label: Procurement and integration
items: MOQ 5,000 pieces; lead time 12-18 business days; per-tag cost USD 0.30-0.90 depending on inlay size and chip variant.
AES-128 key provisioning at NXP secure facility — coordinated through Proud Tek as part of first production batch.
Brand-side integration: backend verification API + branded verification page; CPNP notification ID + MoCRA facility ID encoded in SDM payload.

US MoCRA 2022 + FDA cosmetics facility registration.

heroPoints: Ultra-compact NTAG 424 DNA inlays (Ø 18 mm round, 12 × 19 mm rectangular) on flexible PET conform to curved bottle, compact, jar, tube surfaces without detuning the NFC antenna. Transparent PET overlay + clear adhesive minimise visual impact on premium packaging — preserve the unboxing experience while adding cryptographic security layer.

AES-128 + Secure Dynamic Messaging per-tap unique CMAC URL — counterfeits cannot reproduce the per-tap signature without extracting the AES-128 key from chip silicon (impractical at any normal adversary budget). Defeats super-fake counterfeits that have reached visual near-parity with genuine cosmetics packaging.

EU Cosmetic Products Regulation 1223/2009 + CPNP notification cross-reference encoded in SDM payload + US MoCRA 2022 facility-registration ID + Article 23 SUE (serious undesirable events) consumer-facing reporting flow — single chip serves authentication, regulatory cross-reference, and adverse-event reporting on the branded tap page.

sections.title: Why beauty brands need cryptographic authentication, not visual security
bullets: Counterfeit cosmetics frequently contain lead, mercury, arsenic, bacteria — direct consumer-safety hazard. A single contaminated batch under a genuine brand's label generates lawsuits, regulatory investigations, lasting brand damage.
Visual security features (holograms, serial stickers, batch codes) replicable within weeks of launch; consumers cannot distinguish counterfeit from genuine by visual inspection.

Small curved containers limit label surface — bulky holograms / thick tamper labels compromise the packaging aesthetics premium beauty brands depend on. Compact PET inlays preserve the design language.

sections.title: From hologram + serial 2000s to NFC + CPNP / MoCRA cosmetics default

items.label: 2000s-2010s
items.text: Premium cosmetics anti-counterfeit relies on holograms + foil-stamped seals + serial-number stickers + batch codes — visual security features replicable within weeks of launch by sophisticated counterfeiters.
EU Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 publishes (effective 2013); Cosmetic Products Notification Portal (CPNP) operationalises notifying-authority workflow + Responsible Person framework.
Apple Pay launches with NFC reader on iPhone 6; consumer-scale NFC tap normalises. NTAG family commoditises HF NFC silicon at price points compatible with mass-market cosmetics.
{chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} launches with AES-128 SUN. Premium cosmetics early adopters (luxury fragrance, prestige skincare) begin pilot programmes — Estée Lauder, La Mer, La Prairie, Chanel, Dior.

U.S. Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act (MoCRA) enacted — first major modernisation since 1938. FDA-administered facility registration, product listing, safety substantiation, adverse-event reporting framework.
EU Regulation 2024/1781 ESPR Digital Product Passport publishes; cosmetics likely future DPP category. NFC + CPNP integration positions cosmetics brands ahead of expanded regulatory framework.

items.label: 2026 Today
items.text: Field-reference patterns drawn from prestige-cosmetics-counter, e-commerce-cosmetics-verification, hair-care-professional-only, fragrance-anti-refill, and K-beauty-export programmes converge on NTAG 424 DNA silicon + ultra-compact flexible PET inlay (Ø 18 / 12 × 19 mm) + transparent overlay for visual integration + CPNP notification ID + MoCRA facility ID encoded in SDM payload + branded consumer-tap page with full INCI + adverse-event reporting + recall targeting as the operator-side template.

sections.title: How a tap becomes proof — the SUN authentication flow
sections.intro: The label does not store a password a counterfeiter could read off it. Each tap makes the NTAG 424 DNA chip sign a fresh URL with an AES-128 key that never leaves the silicon — so a copied link works exactly once, then reports itself on the next tap. The chip-level mechanics are in the [NTAG 424 DNA SUN + CMAC encyclopedia](/guides/ntag424-dna-sun-cmac-authentication/).

image.alt: Four-step tap-to-verify flow: phone taps at 13.56 MHz, NTAG 424 DNA emits a fresh per-tap CMAC URL with its AES-128 key, the brand server verifies the signature, and the result shows genuine — a copied URL returns counterfeit on the next tap.

bullets: Secure Dynamic Messaging (SDM) makes the chip emit a new CMAC URL on every tap — replay of a captured URL is caught by the server's tap counter.
The AES-128 key is provisioned into the silicon at NXP's secure facility and never leaves it; cloning the packaging does not clone the key.
The consumer needs no app — the phone OS opens the returned URL and the branded page shows genuine, ingredient data, or a recall alert.
EU CPNP notification ID and US MoCRA facility ID ride in the same SDM payload, so one tap serves authentication and regulatory cross-reference.

sections.title: Built for curved packaging — flexible PET, near-invisible, tamper-evident
sections.intro: Premium packaging is mostly curves, and a rigid inlay detunes the moment it wraps a bottle. A flexible-PET inlay conforms to the glass, hides under a transparent overlay, and — where the box seal needs it — voids on removal. The general-purpose sibling is the [NTAG 424 DNA TamperTag](/products/rfid-labels/ntag424-dna-tamper-evident-tag/).

bullets: Flexible PET conforms to cylindrical bottles, jars and tubes without detuning the antenna — the structural advantage over rigid inlays.
A transparent PET overlay and clear adhesive keep the label near-invisible; embed under an opaque label for a fully hidden placement.
Tamper-evident adhesive leaves a VOID pattern on the outer-box seal; a bridge-antenna closure variant breaks the trace when a refill bottle is opened.
Standard sizes: Ø 22 mm (25-35 mm read), Ø 18 mm (20-30 mm), 12 × 19 mm (15-25 mm); below Ø 12 mm, move the tag to the outer carton.

faq.question: Will the NFC label work through glass bottles?
faq.answer: Yes — NFC signals at 13.56 MHz pass through glass with minimal attenuation. Labels applied to outside of glass bottles (under the paper label or on the bottom) read normally. For labels placed inside packaging, NFC signal passes through cardboard, paper, most plastics. Metal foil packaging blocks the signal — position the label outside any metallic layers.

faq.question: Can the label be made invisible on transparent packaging?
faq.answer: Nearly invisible — Proud Tek uses transparent PET overlay films and clear adhesive to minimise visual impact on clear packaging. The NFC antenna pattern (thin aluminium coil) is subtly visible on close inspection but blends into most packaging designs. For fully invisible placement, embed the inlay under an opaque label or inside the packaging structure.

faq.question: What if a consumer's phone doesn't have NFC?
faq.answer: Recommend printing a small QR code near the NFC label as fallback. QR code links to the same verification page. While QR codes lack NFC's cryptographic security (a QR can be copied), they provide backup for the small percentage of phones without NFC capability. Over 90% of smartphones sold today include NFC.

faq.question: How does the NFC label interact with EU Cosmetic Products Regulation 1223/2009 and the CPNP?
faq.answer: EU Regulation 1223/2009 requires every cosmetic product placed on EU market notified to Cosmetic Products Notification Portal (CPNP) and to carry Responsible Person identity, ingredient list (INCI), batch code, PAO (period after opening) symbol on label or package. These disclosures must remain on physical packaging — NFC tag does not substitute for the regulatory on-pack label. NFC adds: (a) consumer-facing extended-information layer with full INCI + allergen highlighting + safety-assessment summaries + CPNP notification reference, (b) batch-level recall targeting under Article 6 post-market surveillance, (c) Responsible Person contact path for Article 23 SUE (serious undesirable effects) reporting. CPNP notification ID encoded in SDM payload — consumer page cross-references against EU public CPNP lookup.

faq.question: How small can the inlay go before NFC read distance is unusable?
faq.answer: At 13.56 MHz, read distance scales roughly with antenna area; smaller antennas deliver shorter read distances. Smallest standard inlay (Ø 12 mm round, for lipstick tubes / lip-gloss caps) reads reliably at 5-10 mm from a modern smartphone — enough for confirmed consumer tap but not for backroom inventory scanning. 12 × 19 mm rectangular reads at 15-25 mm; Ø 18 mm round reads at 20-30 mm. Below Ø 12 mm (Ø 8 mm experimental antennas exist for solid-perfume compacts and lip balm sticks), read reliability drops below the 95% first-tap success threshold required for consumer-facing deployments. For ultra-small containers, place tag on outer carton or neck-card pendant rather than shrinking the antenna.

faq.question: How does this work with US MoCRA 2022 cosmetics regulation?
faq.answer: Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA) — FDA-administered facility registration, product listing, safety substantiation, and adverse-event reporting (serious adverse events within 15 business days). NFC adds consumer-facing complaint / adverse-event reporting flow on the branded tap page; facility-registration ID encoded in SDM payload for FDA traceability cross-reference. EU CPNP and US MoCRA can both be encoded on the same chip — branded tap page surfaces region-appropriate regulatory information based on phone locale.

faq.question: What is the MOQ, lead time and sample process for cosmetics authentication labels?
faq.answer: MOQ is 5,000 pieces, lead time 12-18 business days, and per-tag cost USD 0.30-0.90 depending on inlay size and chip variant. AES-128 key provisioning happens at NXP's secure facility, coordinated as part of the first production batch, so plan a sampling round before the production run. Blank and pre-encoded inlay samples are available for antenna-fit testing on your specific bottle, jar or compact before you commit to tooling.
